stem: Which of the following values of \(x\) satisfies both \(x > -3\) and \(x \le 1\)?
solution: A value works only if it is greater than \(-3\) and also at most 1.
\(-3\) is not greater than \(-3\), \(-5\) is less than \(-3\), and \(2\) is greater than 1.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The first inequality is strict: \(-3\) is not greater than \(-3\), so it is not a solution.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(-5 < -3\), so \(-5\) fails \(x > -3\). This comes from reading \(x > -3\) as \(x < -3\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(2 > 1\), so 2 fails \(x \le 1\). The second inequality allows 1 itself but nothing larger.

verify:
ok = [k for k, c in choices.items() if value(c) > -3 and value(c) <= 1]
assert ok == [answer]
